newsitem.title: FRANCE: New strikes to hit French planes and trains.
newsitem.headline: New strikes to hit French planes and trains.

text.p: French air traffic faces further disruption this weekend and many trains will be cancelled from Wednesday as unions strike over pay and work status.

Traffic controllers at France's SNCF national railways said they would strike from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Wednesday until 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) on Friday because of what they called inadequate management proposals about the future of their jobs.

SNCF management said one train in three would run nationally except on the Eurostar lines and the Paris-Rouen-Le Havre and Paris-Cherbourg runs, which would not be affected. Paris suburban trains would suffer from lighter disruption. SNCF said.

Pilots at Air France Europe, the European unit of national carrier Air France, said they would strike on Friday and Saturday over the merging of staff seniority lists at the two airlines, operating as one company since April 1.

Pilots at Air France Europe, also known as Air Inter Europe, said combining the lists under the current proposal would make them lose about five years seniority compared to Air France pilots with similar service records.
A strike at TAT-Air Liberte, French units of British Airways Plc, dragged on despite the return to work of some Air Liberte pilots.
Pilots at TAT and flight attendants at both airlines are protesting over their merger, which they say is detrimental to their work conditions.
